_doc.what: Scripted traceroute paths for demo/bin/traceroute and demo/bin/ping.

<dest-ip>.kind: multihop | routechange | refused | silent | dead | degraded
<dest-ip>.hops: [[addr, base_rtt_ms], ...] in TTL order, index 0 == TTL 1. addr null means the hop never answers (prints '* * *'); base_rtt_ms is the median RTT the shim jitters around.
<dest-ip>.alt_hops: optional {"<ttl>": [addr, base_rtt_ms]} - routechange swaps these in on alternate runs, and occasionally prints both the primary and the alternate on one hop line.
<dest-ip>.annotate: optional {"<ttl>": "!X"} - ICMP unreachable annotation printed after every probe RTT at that TTL. The trace stops after an annotated hop, exactly as traceroute(8) does.
<dest-ip>.loss_probes: optional {"<ttl>": N} - N of the -q probes at that TTL print '*' instead of an RTT.
<dest-ip>.stop_after: optional 1-based TTL after which no further hop lines are printed (used by 'refused').
<dest-ip>.notes: free text, for humans reading the file

kinds.multihop: clean path, destination answers at the final hop
kinds.routechange: hop 2 flips between two addresses across invocations, so TraceResult.path_signature() changes
kinds.refused: a router answers with an ICMP administratively-prohibited annotation and the trace ends there; never reached
kinds.silent: one mid-path hop is fully silent ('* * *') but the destination still answers
kinds.dead: nothing answers at any TTL, up to -m
kinds.degraded: destination answers, but with high RTT and one lost probe of three

conventions: Every destination is a numeric IP because netpath.tracer.run_trace() resolves the host with gethostbyname() before running the binary.
Any 127.x.y.z destination is handled without a routes.json entry: a single hop that is the destination itself.
A destination not listed here behaves like 'dead'.
RTT jitter is seeded from int(time.time() // 60), so repeated runs inside a minute are identical and consecutive minutes look alive but similar.
demo/bin/ping answers for every non-null hop address that appears below, and for 127.x; everything else is 100% loss with exit status 1.

10.0.0.1.notes: Healthy four-hop path to the core. The baseline every other destination is compared against.

10.0.0.2.notes: Equal-cost pair at TTL 2. Flips every 3 invocations, and every 7th invocation prints both addresses on the one hop line the way traceroute does when probes land on different routers.

10.0.0.3.notes: A firewall at 10.0.9.1 answers with administratively-prohibited. reached=False, unreachable_code='!X', unreachable_from='10.0.9.1'.

10.0.0.4.notes: A transit router with ICMP TTL-exceeded rate-limited off. Hop 3 is '* * *' but the destination still answers at hop 6, so reached=True with a gap in the middle.

10.0.0.5.notes: Nothing answers anywhere. Every TTL up to -m prints '* * *'; reached=False and there is no unreachable code to explain it.

10.0.0.6.notes: Reached, but the destination hop is ~180 ms and drops one probe of three - enough for netpath_latency_high without ever looking unreachable.
